title: 「According to」引述資料來源句
titleEn: Using according to to attribute information to a source

source.file: Sentence Structure 138 -「According to」引述資料來源句.pdf
omissions: English versions of Chinese-only Important Rules and Benefits headings are faithful editorial translations.

formula: According to + person / document / information source, + complete sentence

formulas.formula: According to + person / document / information source, + complete sentence
Complete sentence, according to + person / document / information source

example: According to the weather forecast, it will rain tomorrow.
exampleZh: 根據天氣預報，明天會下雨。

examples.en: According to the weather forecast, it will rain tomorrow.
examples.zh: 根據天氣預報，明天會下雨。

rules.zh: According to 後面接名詞或名詞詞組 正確： 錯誤： 不可同時使用 according to 和 says 來引入同一個來源。
rules.en: According to is followed by a noun or noun phrase. Do not use according to and says together to introduce the same source.
examples: According to the teacher, the test will be difficult.

rules.zh: 主句必須完整 正確： 錯誤： 在逗號後面必須有完整的主語和動詞。
rules.en: The main clause must be complete, with a full subject and verb after the comma.

rules.zh: According to 通常不用來表達自己的意見 不自然： 表達自己的看法時，通常使用： According to 通常用來引述其他人或外部資料來源。
rules.en: Do not normally use according to to introduce your own opinion. Use an expression such as in my opinion for your view; according to normally attributes a statement to another person or an external source.
examples: In my opinion, the plan is unfair.

rules.zh: 資料來源可以是人物或文件 人物 文件或資料
rules.en: The source may be a person, such as a teacher, manager, doctor or named individual, or a document or data source, such as a report, timetable, website, figures or instructions.

rules.zh: According to 可以放在句首或句末 句首： 句末： 句首形式較能突出資料來源；句末形式則先突出主要消息。
rules.en: According to may appear at the beginning or end. Initial position foregrounds the source, while final position foregrounds the main information.

rules.zh: According to 與 Based on 的分別 According to：指出「資料來自哪裏」 這句是在報告天氣預報所提供的消息。 Based on：指出「決定或判斷以甚麼為依據」 這句是在說明我們作出取消決定的依據。 簡單分辨方法 是誰說的？資料來自哪裏？ 這個決定或結論以甚麼證據為基礎？ 因此： 兩者不能在所有情況下互相替換。
rules.en: According to attributes information by answering ‘Who or what says this?’ or ‘Where does the information come from?’. Based on identifies the evidence used for a decision or conclusion. Thus according to reports what a forecast says, whereas based on explains why a decision was made, and the two cannot be interchanged in every context.
examples: According to = Who or what says this?
Based on = What evidence caused this decision or conclusion?
According to the weather forecast, heavy rain is expected.
Based on the weather forecast, we cancelled the picnic.
According to customer feedback, many users find the app confusing.
We redesigned the app based on customer feedback.

benefits.zh: 清楚交代消息來源 這個句型能讓讀者立即知道資料是由誰提供，或來自哪一份文件。 讀者清楚知道這是醫生提供的消息，而不是說話者自己的判斷。
benefits.en: It clearly identifies the source of information, showing immediately who supplied it or which document contains it and distinguishing that source’s report from the speaker’s own judgement.

benefits.zh: 幫助分開「自己的意見」和「別人的說法」 使用 According to 可以避免把外部資料說成自己的看法，使表達更加準確和可靠。
benefits.en: It separates your own opinion from somebody else’s statement, preventing external information from being presented as your own view and making the message more accurate and reliable.

benefits.zh: 把來源和消息連成一句 不用分開寫： 可以寫成： 句子更直接，也更容易理解。
benefits.en: It connects a source and its information in one direct, easy-to-understand sentence instead of splitting the source and message into separate statements.

benefits.zh: 適合學校、工作和日常溝通 你可以用它引述： ● 老師的指示； ● 公司通知； ● 新聞報道； ● 調查結果； ● 時間表； ● 醫生的建議； ● 網站資料。
benefits.en: It is useful at school, at work and in everyday communication for citing teachers’ instructions, company notices, news reports, survey results, timetables, doctors’ advice and website information.

benefits.zh: 增加句子的組織和變化 你可以把 According to + source 放在句首，先介紹資料來源；也可以放在句末，先說出最重要 的消息。 這能避免每句都以人物或事物作為開頭。
benefits.en: It improves organization and sentence variety. Put According to + source first to introduce the source before the message, or place it last to foreground the most important news; either choice avoids beginning every sentence with a person or thing.
